title: Red alert in nine districts in Kerala, death toll rises to six
content: Heavy rain continued to batter large parts of Kerala, particularly the central districts, early on Saturday, triggering landslides, flooding and widespread waterlogging. A red alert has been declared in nine districts. The IMD has predicted extreme rainfall in Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur, Kasaragod, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, and Thrissur. Ranni town was completely flooded in the heavy showers. A woman was killed after a landslide triggered by incessant rain buried a house at Adurmala in Kudayathoor, near Thodupuzha, in Idukki district. The deceased was identified as Sumathi, a resident of Mashikkallel House in Ward 7 of Kudayathoor. Her body was recovered around 7 am after an extensive search operation that began in the early hours of Saturday. Her husband, Ravi, and their son, Ratheesh, sustained injuries and were rescued from the debris. The landslide struck around 2 am, completely burying and destroying the family's house. In a second incident, Prabhakaran Nair (72), a native of Vaikom, was killed after a huge mass of earth crashed through the window of the room where he was sleeping at his relative's house, Pournami Nivas, in Kolahalamedu, Vagamon. Prabhakaran, uncle of the house owner Leelamani, had arrived at the house only a day earlier. His room was completely buried under mud and debris, while Leelamani, who was in an adjacent room, escaped unhurt. Fire and Rescue Services personnel, police, and local residents carried out a rescue operation for several hours before recovering the body at around 10.30 am. An earthmover was used to remove part of the house and clear the debris. Vagamon police have initiated further proceedings, and the body will be handed over to the family after the post-mortem examination. Meanwhile, a youth, identified as Joseph Johnny and his mother, Regina Johnny, died in a landslide that occurred at Poonjar around 3 am. At Mathayippara in Upputhara, another landslide hit a police jeep. Fortunately, the police personnel had stepped out of the vehicle moments earlier and escaped unhurt. Two minor landslides were also reported at Nellappara in Karinkunnam, though no casualties were reported. In Kottayam district, a landslide occurred near the Mankombu Temple area in Moonnilavu. In Pathanamthitta district, landslides were reported from several hilly areas as heavy rain continued through the night. Holiday for educational institutions In view of the inclement weather, district collectors of Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Malappuram, Palakkad and Idukki declared a holiday for all educational institutions on Saturday. The holiday applies to schools, professional colleges, anganwadis, tuition centres, coaching centres, special classes and madrassas. However, examinations and interviews scheduled earlier will be held as planned. Orange alert in five districts The IMD has issued an orange alert for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Alappuzha, Ernakulam, and Palakkad with a warning of very heavy rainfall between 12 cm and 20 cm within 24 hours. Flooding and waterlogging Heavy rain triggered flooding and waterlogging across several districts, with Idukki, Kottayam and Pathanamthitta among the worst affected. In Kottayam, the Mundakkayam Causeway Bridge was submerged after water levels rose sharply. Erattupetta town was inundated after the Meenachil River overflowed its banks. Several stretches of the Pala-Poonjar Road also went under water, disrupting traffic. In Pathanamthitta, rainwater flooded the Ittiyappara bus stand in Ranni as heavy rain continued overnight. In Idukki, overflowing streams and rivers inundated roads and residential areas at multiple locations. At Vandiperiyar, streams overflowed and water entered sections of the KK Road, though traffic remained unaffected.
